layers.rank_note: 3 congressional districts — the largest districts Nebraska carries below the state itself

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 3 features for Nebraska, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 3 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Nebraska Legislature District
layers.rank_note: 49 legislative districts, each electing one senator to Nebraska's one-chamber Legislature

source.answers: The legislative district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 49 features. Nebraska's Legislature has one chamber, and TIGERweb carries its districts on the upper-chamber layer and nothing on the lower-chamber layer, so the one map is simplified on its own, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ne-legislature-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Legislature's own pages (nebraskalegislature.gov, the senator list and each district's senator page): each senator's name, e-mail address at leg.ne.gov, the one telephone the page prints and page. Nebraska elects its senators on a ballot that names no party, so no party is carried. The site states a Crawl-delay of 3 seconds, which the builder honours.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 93 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 93 features, measured 2026-11-12. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each Nebraska county is governed by an elected board of commissioners or, where the county kept township government, a board of supervisors, and also elects officers such as a clerk, a treasurer, an assessor, a sheriff and a county attorney. No list of them was read in this pass, so the card says how the county is governed and names nobody. Recorded as gap ne-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 244 school districts, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 244 features for Nebraska, measured 2026-11-12: 244 school districts, every one running pre-kindergarten to grade 12. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Nebraska, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap ne-school-board-members.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 592 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Nebraska (877 in the app's bounding box), about 336 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Nebraska (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='31'. The app's box reaches into South Dakota, Iowa, Missouri, Kansas, Colorado and Wyoming, and measured 2026-11-12, 592 of the 877 ZCTAs in it reach into Nebraska and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Nebraska. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City or Village
layers.rank_note: 528 incorporated cities and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 528 records: 381 villages and 147 cities, every one an active government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF NEBRASKA IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY OR VILLAGE (about 1% of its land, 2,092.9 of 198,950.7 km2, is inside one), and the county, with the township in the 20 counties that kept township government, is the local government everywhere else, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. The Census's census-designated places are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn. The state's county subdivisions are precincts, which have no government, and in the 20 counties that kept township government, townships: 319 of them the Census records as active governments (measured 2026-11-12). The townships are not drawn yet.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Nebraska's local officials was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ne-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Nebraska has 9 pieces held by seven nations, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py on 2026-11-13, with the counties measured against this app's own county outlines: the Omaha Reservation (787.1 km² in Nebraska, 98.0% of it, Thurston, Cuming and Burt counties), the Santee Reservation (477.9 km², Knox County), the Winnebago Reservation (457.5 km² in Nebraska, 99.4% of it, Thurston and Dixon counties) and its trust land (0.465 km², Burt County), the Ponca (NE) Trust Land (0.825 km², Knox County), the Sac and Fox Nation Reservation (40.0 km² in Nebraska) and trust land (0.431 km²) and the Iowa (KS-NE) Reservation (15.6 km² in Nebraska), all three in Richardson County, and 2.236 km² of the Pine Ridge Reservation in Sheridan County. Every piece but the Santee Reservation and the Winnebago trust land is drawn whole across the state line. The Census draws one tribal district on the Pine Ridge land in Nebraska. Ranked after municipalities and before the point layers, as Nevada's and Arizona's are, so they are drawn above the larger areas around them. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — Nebraska has 9 such areas, held by seven nations: the Omaha Tribe, the Santee Sioux Nation, the Winnebago Tribe and the Ponca Tribe, all seated in Nebraska, the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska and the Sac & Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska, seated in Kansas, and the Oglala Sioux Tribe, seated in South Dakota.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: The Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska's council of nine, from the tribe's own page (the list Iowa's card names for the reservation's Iowa part), re-read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py into data/app/tribal-councils.json and named with the date it was read. The Omaha Tribe's site could not be reached from where this project is built (2026-10-10), so its card says so (ROSTER_BLOCKED in scripts/build_tribal_areas.py); this app has not yet read the council lists the other five nations publish, so their cards say so and link each nation's own site (ROSTER_NOT_SOUGHT). The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Nebraska — the 9 pieces of land above, in Thurston, Cuming, Burt, Dixon, Knox, Richardson and Sheridan counties. Every other point in the state is on no tribal land the Census draws for a government.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 268 points in Nebraska's envelope, which reaches into South Dakota, Iowa, Missouri, Kansas, Colorado and Wyoming; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Nebraska — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Nebraska State Capitol, 1445 K Street, Lincoln, Lancaster County

negative_point.note: Clay County, South Dakota, north of the Missouri River — outside Nebraska and inside permalink_gate, so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names South Dakota here (control: the Nebraska State Capitol returns Nebraska), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and of every outline in the fleet only South Dakota's does (South Dakota goes live in the same change as Nebraska). Nebraska borders no water and no other country, and every one of its neighbours (South Dakota, Iowa, Missouri, Kansas, Colorado and Wyoming) is live once this change lands, so no point this app's gate reaches lies outside every instance: the point stays where it is, as Illinois's sits in Indiana's waters, and a selection the app makes from its own link never leaves for another app.

geometry.note: The whole-Nebraska outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (93 counties).
Nebraska's 93 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 3 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 49 districts of Nebraska's one-chamber Legislature, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper).

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Nebraska's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — six reservations and three pieces of off-reservation trust land, seven pieces drawn whole across the state line, the Pine Ridge Reservation among them, at the Census's own detail (260 KB). The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-11-13; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The council of the Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska, from its own page, keyed by the Census AIANNH code of its land (4625) — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). The same council Iowa's card names for the reservation's Iowa part. Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.

The officers Nebraska elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from ne/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
